newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Athletic Park revamp cost tops $650,000.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Athletic Park revamp cost tops $650,000.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Sept 27 - It will cost about $200,000 more than earlier estimated to bring Athletic Park up to scratch for next year's Argentina-All Black rugby test, NZPA reported on Friday.

The final figure -- $650,000 -- worries Wellington Mayor Mark Blumsky, who met Wellington Rugby Football Union (WRFU) chairman Murray McCaw, deputy chairman Dave Smith and WRFU board member Peter Allport yesterday to talk about rugby's future in the capital.

Changes to the park have been requested by the New Zealand Rugby Football Union to accommodate players in the professional era. If minimum standards are not met, tests will be taken away from Wellington.

The WRFU is struggling to find the money to fund the improvements. It was nearly $100,000 behind its gate budget before last Saturday's Auckland match and a serious shortfall in the more expensive $20 seating area has meant a deficit of nearly $25,000 for that game.
Blumsky today would not comment on whether Wellington City Council would contribute money.
"I sympathise with the Wellington union with their problems and I hope they look at all corners of society to assist them with the funding," he said.
"It's important that Athletic Park be developed by March -- top rugby is worth far too much for the city to be allowed to go from the park.
"At present, we're looking at the (year) 2000 rugby season before rugby will be on at the new stadium and that's four years of top-class rugby which can't be allowed to leave the city.
"That would have a huge impact on the financial state of the city. We're talking millions of dollars to Wellington here," Blumsky said.
The required changes include two new gates -- the A gate at the north end of the main stand, and the E gate entrance behind the Millard Stand.
Two new dressing rooms are planned under the main stand. One is planned at the stand's south end, at present used as a storage area, and the second would be on the eastern side of the stand corridor.
The present Nos 1 and 2 dressing rooms would be used only by teams playing curtain-raisers.
Neither McCaw nor Smith were available for comment early today.
